situation:
You are the client services manager at CROSSTOWN ATHLETE PARTNERS, a sports agency and athlete representation firm. The managing partner (judge) has asked you to recommend what the agency should do about the free Saturday skills clinics it runs for young athletes, and to explain how that recommendation would be presented to the community partner who runs the clinics alongside the agency.

The agency is two years old and represents eighteen professional athletes. It has never bought a broadcast spot, a billboard, or any other paid advertising. Nearly every client it has signed came from a parent or a coach who watched one of its athletes work with children at the clinics, which the agency runs with the CITY PARKS ALLIANCE under a four-year agreement. Its first round of funding runs out in five months.

A sports drink company has offered the agency one hundred forty thousand dollars to turn the clinics into a ticketed regional showcase filmed for its social channels. Accepting the money means charging families a ninety-five dollar entry fee for what has always been free, and moving the clinics out of the neighborhood parks, which ends the four-year agreement with the CITY PARKS ALLIANCE.

Turning the offer down keeps the clinics free and the agreement with the alliance intact, but the agency would then enter its final five months of funding with no new revenue and would have to cut the athlete appearance travel that brings its clients to the clinics in the first place. The alliance director has already called twice, complaining that families heard about the entry fee before she did.

The managing partner (judge) wants your recommendation on whether to accept the offer, how the agency should answer the complaints coming from the alliance director and from families, and what the clinics do for the agency that paid advertising would not. The managing partner (judge) will greet you in the office and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the managing partner (judge) will thank you for your work.
